title: BIO, NIO and AIO
context: What is the difference between BIO, NIO and AIO?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: BIO (blocking I/O) uses one thread per connection. Each read or write blocks that thread. NIO (non-blocking I/O) uses channels and selectors, so one thread can watch many connections and handle only the ready ones. AIO (asynchronous I/O, NIO.2) starts an operation and gets a callback or future when it completes. Servers such as Netty build on NIO's selector model. For most backend code, use a framework that already implements NIO.

points.title: Threads per connection
points.why: BIO needs a thread per connection, which limits how many clients one server can hold.

points.title: Selectors
points.why: NIO uses a selector so one thread can handle many ready connections.
